picks.rationale: The AIntibody Challenge is the first blinded, prospective wet-lab test of AI-designed antibodies — a hard reality check on generative protein design, published in Nature Biotechnology.
picks.excerpt: Researchers affiliated with UTHealth Houston, competing as Novamab AI, placed among the top five teams in the international AIntibody Challenge, a blinded, prospective benchmark published in Nature Biotechnology. It is one of the first hard tests of whether AI-designed antibodies actually bind their targets in the lab.

picks.rationale: CrysVCD bolts chemical-valence constraints onto generative crystal models, so the designs that come out are synthesizable instead of screened away later.
picks.excerpt: MIT researchers added a new component to AI models that design new materials, helping ensure the material will be stable and practical for real-world use. The CrysVCD approach could reduce the money and time spent screening out unusable generated designs.

picks.rationale: HydroGym is an open RL benchmark for flow control, and controllers trained on toy channel flows transferred to a wing sim — concrete evidence that learned control generalizes.
picks.excerpt: HydroGym, an open reinforcement-learning proving ground from Washington, Michigan and German groups, trains and benchmarks AI controllers for fluid flow. Controllers trained on simple channel flows transferred to a wing simulation, cutting surface friction 38% and drag 11%.

picks.rationale: Cognitive scientists are reverse-engineering why a child needs orders of magnitude less data than an LLM — the clearest current line between developmental science and model efficiency.
picks.excerpt: LLMs need vastly more data than children to learn language. Cognitive scientists are reverse-engineering that data-efficiency gap in the hope of building far more efficient models — and learning something about developing minds.

picks.rationale: Classical tensor networks beat a quantum annealer on Ising spin glasses — another data point that learned classical solvers keep moving the quantum-advantage goalposts.
picks.excerpt: Classical tensor-network computation proved more accurate than a quantum annealer for some Ising spin glasses, another data point in the contest between learned classical solvers and quantum hardware.
